dimensions.reason: Privacy Procedure (N084, 6.1-6.4) explicitly covers automated systems analysing personal information to support educational and service-related functions, alongside purpose limitation (5.1) and access/correction (4.3-4.4). However, it does not explicitly address persistent cross-course AI learner profiles or whether instructors must be notified of their scope.

6. Automated Decision-Making
6.1 The University may use automated systems or tools to assist in decision
making processes. These may include analysing personal information to
support administrative, educational, research, or service-related functions.
6.2 Where an automated decision-making process is used, the University will:
6.2.1 ensure the use of personal information complies with the PRIS Act,
including the IPPs;
6.2.2 take reasonable steps to ensure that any automated decision is fair,
accurate, and based on reliable and up to date information;
6.2.3 provide individuals with information about the use of automated
decision making where it forms a substantial part of a decision that
affects them;
6.2.4 ensure that a meaningful human review is available upon request
where an automated process has materially influenced an
outcome; and
6.2.5 maintain appropriate oversight, auditability, and safeguards to
prevent unlawful discrimination, bias, or adverse impacts arising
from automated processes.

6.4 Automated decision making will not be used as the sole basis for decisions
that may significantly affect an individual’s rights, access to services, or
opportunities without appropriate human involvement.

5.1 The general rule is that the University will not use or disclose personal
information other than for the primary purposes for which it was collected.
5.2 The information may be used/disclosed for reasons other than the primary
purpose of collection where the provider of the information has consented;
and/or there is a reasonable expectation of disclosure.

4.3 Upon request, and subject to applicable exceptions, the University will
provide access to the personal information it holds about an individual
within 30 days, at no cost. Personal information may be reviewed and
depending on its nature, may be updated or corrected in accordance with
relevant procedures. This applies, for example, to information held on
Callista (MyInfo) for students and Workday for staff. Access may be denied

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Informed purpose and cross-course use, accountable lifecycle ownership, access/correction and contestability of consequential profiling.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: While N084 (6.1-6.4, 4.3-4.4) provides strong access/correction and automated-decision contestability rights, no operative rule governs cross-course/cross-semester AI learner-profile lifecycle ownership or instructor transparency when a persistent profile influences assessment and advising.
case_summary.case_note: Murdoch's Privacy Procedure (N084, 6.1-6.4) explicitly regulates automated decision-making, requiring notice, bias auditability, meaningful human review upon request, and prohibiting sole automated decisions affecting rights or services, alongside 30-day free access and correction (4.3-4.4). However, no policy assigns lifecycle ownership for persistent cross-course AI learner profiles or ensures instructor visibility when profiles span units, leaving a critical gap. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15, and this proposal awaits human verification.
